cf.title: Two fixes for parallel query cleanup: DSM detach order and a stray statement timeout

input.subject: Two fixes for parallel query cleanup: DSM detach order and a stray statement timeout

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the panel, so nothing stops either patch at levels 1a, 1b or 2. Both are bug fixes with measured reproducers, and 0002 restores the behaviour before 22f6f2c1ccb. Confidence is low because only message #1 is visible, no one has replied, and two safety points need the code.

brief.title: Parallel query cleanup: detach DSM after workers exit, clear stray statement timeout
brief.problem: A user who cancels a parallel query gets errors in the log from workers that start after the leader detached the DSM segment. A statement_timeout that fires during end-of-query cleanup, such as temp file deletion in dsm_detach() with interrupts held, stays pending and cancels the next statement, even a COMMIT.
brief.proposed_design: 0001 moves dsm_detach() in DestroyParallelContext() to after WaitForParallelWorkersToExit(), but still detaches the error queues before the wait. 0002 changes disable_statement_timeout() so it clears the fired indicator and the queued cancel request when the timer has fired but was not serviced. The patches are independent.
user_visible_surface: Cancelled parallel queries no longer log errors from workers that fail to map the segment or attach to the DSA or SharedFileSet.
A statement_timeout that fires after a statement's last CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS() no longer cancels the next statement.
author_claims: Cancelling a 4-worker parallel hash join 1200 times logged 407 errors on master and none with 0001.
With 0001, cancelling workers blocked on full tuple queues, parallel CREATE INDEX and parallel VACUUM showed no hang and no leftover temp files.
Without 0002, a follow-up statement failed 5 of 120 times, and COMMIT failed 4 of 242 times, leaving an aborted transaction block; with 0002 both counts drop to zero.
0002 fixes a regression from 22f6f2c1ccb present in 13 and later, and restores the earlier behaviour; Tom described the case in [2].
The REPACK decoding worker copied the same shutdown sequence, and its early dsm_detach() was fixed separately.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. No one has replied.
unclear: The material does not say whether clearing a fired but unserviced timeout can drop a cancel request that should still apply, such as a user cancel.
The author does not say whether 0002 also covers lock_timeout, idle timeouts or other timeouts with the same pattern.
The author does not say whether either patch is meant for back branches.
The material does not say whether 0001 changes cleanup when a worker never exits or the postmaster dies during the wait.
The reproducer is attached but not described, so the timing setup is not shown.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #1 calls 0002 a regression in 13 and later but does not say which branches either patch targets.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Both patches change cleanup ordering and interrupt bookkeeping in parallel.c and postgres.c, where timing bugs are hard to reproduce.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: 0002 changes disable_statement_timeout(), which runs once per statement; no added cost is claimed or shown.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Can 0002 clear a cancel request from a client cancel or pg_cancel_backend() that arrives in the same window as the fired statement timeout?
With 0001, what does the leader do with the DSM segment if a worker never exits or the postmaster dies during WaitForParallelWorkersToExit()?
Do lock_timeout, transaction_timeout or the idle timeouts have the same fired-but-unserviced case, and does 0002 cover them?
Which back branches is each patch meant for, given that 0002 is described as a regression in 13 and later?
How does the attached reproducer set up the timing, so that a reviewer can repeat the 5 in 120 and 4 in 242 failure counts?

committability.owner_note: 0001 needs someone who knows parallel context shutdown and DSM lifetime. 0002 needs someone who knows the timeout and interrupt handling in postgres.c.
committability.liability: The committer signs for cleanup ordering in every parallel query and for cancel handling at the end of every statement. If 0002 is back-patched, that covers all supported branches from 13.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; only message #1 exists. The author ran stress tests and attached a reproducer.

priority.reason: 0002 fixes a case where a COMMIT fails and leaves an aborted transaction block, for users who combine statement_timeout with parallel queries. Both patches are small and add no user-visible surface, but the timing reasoning needs a reviewer who knows these two areas.

provisional_note: Without the code, the panel could not check whether 0002 clears only the timeout's own cancel request, or whether 0001 keeps the leader safe when a worker never exits. The pass at levels 1 and 2 is provisional on both points.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Cancel problems of query to pg_stat_statements
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_stat_statements queries cancellable by adding interrupt checks inside the read loop of qtext_load_file, which loads the query text file, and by cutting the read chunk size from 1GB to 32MB so the checks run more often. Because the function can run while pgss->lock is held, v2 only records that an interrupt is pending inside the loop and calls CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS after the loop ends and the lock is released.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrey Borodin first noted that the lock held during the file read blocks interrupts anyway; v2 worked around that. Michael Paquier then rejected the patch as only a workaround for a larger problem: the on-disk PGSS query text file does not scale once it is large and entries turn over often. He pointed instead to a planned rework that would move pg_stat_statements onto the pgstats API as a custom stats kind, with the query texts held entirely in memory.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch is only a workaround for a larger problem: the PGSS text
file does not and will never scale once it reaches a large size and
once we have a high turnover rate of the PGSS entries due to different
query IDs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix error message for statement_timeout and fix flaky test
precedents_retrieved.summary: The entry proposed a fix to the statement timeout logic, where a query that hit statement_timeout could report "canceling statement due to user request" instead of a timeout error. It also changed the flaky postgres_fdw cancel test by moving it before use_remote_estimate is enabled and raising its statement_timeout from 10ms to 100ms.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last message, from the author on the day of the decision, posts the test fix and says the test should be removed if failures continue. No objection to either patch appears.

precedents_retrieved.title: timeout parameters in libpq
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patches add a tcp_user_timeout parameter on the server and in libpq that sets the Linux TCP_USER_TIMEOUT socket option. They also add a libpq socket_timeout parameter that closes the connection when a query result does not arrive in time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fabien COELHO's review asked why the server-side statement_timeout is not enough for socket_timeout. He also found that a timeout drops and resets the connection instead of cancelling the query, and that pqWait duplicates pqWaitTimed logic. The patch had no tests and no documentation. Andrei Yahorau warned that the pqWait change breaks callers that expect to wait forever; the author planned new patches after an absence, and the visible thread ends with the review.
matched_queries: spurious canceling statement due to statement timeout
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'd like clarifications about the use case that needs this specific feature, especially to understand why the server-side "statement_timeout" setting is not right enough.

precedents_retrieved.title: pgbench: allow to cancel queries during benchmark
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pgbench send cancel requests to all connections on Ctrl+C, so long-running benchmark queries do not keep running on the backend after pgbench exits. On non-Windows, thread #0 handles SIGINT and cancels queries for all clients through a global array of client states.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fabien COELHO said thread #0 cancelling clients that other threads manage can cause race conditions, and asked that each thread cancel its own clients. In message #19 the author found two more problems: thread #0 cannot cancel anything once it leaves its loop, and with -C each thread recreates its PGcancel objects while thread #0 reads them. Alvaro Herrera then said commit 61461a300c1c, which deprecated PQcancel, requires the patch to be reworked. The author planned a redesign, but the visible messages show no new version.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical replication timeout
precedents_retrieved.summary: A walsender spent hours unlinking every possible spill file name for a large transaction in ReorderBufferRestoreCleanup, so the subscriber timed out and decoding restarted in a loop. The patch records which WAL segments a transaction actually spilled to, so cleanup removes only those files.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last shown message, in March 2025, only reports a rebase. A reviewer had also asked for a second patch that sends progress updates during long loops such as cleanup, and no message shows that patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: GUC to disable cancellation of awaiting for synchronous replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GUC that stops a query cancel from ending the wait for synchronous replication, so a locally committed transaction keeps its locks and stays invisible until a standby confirms it. The goal is to stop clients, including drivers that send a cancel on a query timeout, from seeing data that a failover can lose.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said that blocking cancel does not close the hole, because a server restart or a backend crash also exposes locally committed data that no standby has received. Fujii Masao suggested making new snapshots wait for replication instead, and Andrey Borodin rejected that because of its latency cost. Aleksander Alekseev called the patch a workaround and asked for a community decision, and the visible messages show no agreement before the entry was returned.
matched_queries: spurious canceling statement due to statement timeout
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I don't think that preventing a backend from being canceled during waiting for sync rep actually addresses your issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: minor fix in CancelVirtualTransaction
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the loop in CancelVirtualTransaction to stop scanning once it finds the entry with the matching backendId, even when the localTransactionId does not match and no signal is sent. A later version compares backendId directly with the proc entry and adds a code comment, following review.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author paused the patch because the code has no test coverage and he wanted to write a test first. The test did not arrive, so Andres Freund marked the entry returned with feedback. The reviewer agreed with the change itself.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent matches either patch. [P2] also touches statement_timeout, but it changed which cancel message is reported and fixed a flaky test, and its thread shows no objection that would apply here. Message #1 points to two earlier discussions: [1], where the early dsm_detach() in the REPACK decoding worker was fixed, and [2], where Tom is said to have described the stray-timeout case; the material does not show what either thread decided.

Neither patch changes SQL syntax, GUCs, catalogs, pg_dump output, psql or the wire protocol. 0002 changes visible behaviour only by stopping a spurious statement_timeout error on the next statement, which matches the behaviour before 22f6f2c1ccb. The material does not say whether 0002 can also discard a client cancel request that arrives in the same window. That case is already racy under the current cancel protocol, so it is better left to the safety angle than raised here as a compatibility objection.

Neither patch touches persistent or cross-node state: no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol message or exported struct changes, so pg_upgrade, standbys and back-branch ABI are unaffected. The DSM segment and SharedFileSet temp files are per-query and per-process; the open cleanup question on worker hang or postmaster death needs the code to judge.

Neither patch changes who may do what or what anyone can see. 0001 reorders dsm_detach() after WaitForParallelWorkersToExit() inside the leader's own parallel context, and 0002 changes timeout bookkeeping inside one backend. Neither adds a privilege, a role check, a new exposure path or a resource an unprivileged user can grow without bound. One question belongs to the correctness angle: whether 0002 can drop a pg_cancel_backend() request that arrives in the same window. If that happens, an administrator's cancel would be lost. No one gains access or privileges they did not already have.

From the maintenance and fit angle, neither patch adds a GUC, catalog state, API, dependency or hot-path work. 0001 reorders existing cleanup in one function. 0002 restores how disable_statement_timeout() behaved before 22f6f2c1ccb, and it runs only once per statement. Both are core bug fixes with nothing that could live in an extension. Two points could not be checked without the code and belong to other angles. One is whether 0002 can clear a user cancel that arrives in the same window. The other is whether lock_timeout or transaction_timeout need the same change. Committability: no committer has engaged yet. [P2] touches statement_timeout but records no reason that applies here.

Both patches are bug fixes in core code, parallel.c and the statement timeout handling in postgres.c. No existing feature, setting, extension or hook avoids the stray timeout or the worker attach errors, so nothing from this angle applies. The only precedent, [P2], concerns a different timeout error message and was withdrawn without a recorded objection.

Both patches fix bugs with measured reproducers, so the demand test does not apply in the usual way. 0002 fixes a regression present since 13 that can abort a COMMIT; 0001 removes errors logged after an ordinary cancel; neither adds UI or cost for non-users.
